neighbours.label: comparison word (than / to / with / resembles) after a property-of-X subject, anticipating 'that of'
fire: In many tests the boiling point of ethanol is noticeably lower than that of water at sea level.
Scholars note that the grammar of Maltese is in places similar to that of Arabic.
Her account of the voyage was later compared with that of the ship's surgeon.
The skull shape of this fossil closely resembles that of modern lemurs in several features.
Measured carefully, the output of the new turbine is nearly double that of the old one.
The climate of the northern valley is broadly comparable to that of southern Sweden.
On average the lifespan of a domestic cat is longer than that of a wild one.
Critics felt the plot of the sequel was far weaker than that of the original film.
quiet: In many tests the boiling point of ethanol is measured at sea level in sealed flasks.
Scholars note that the grammar of Maltese has been studied for over a century.
Her account of the voyage was later published by the ship's surgeon.
The skull shape of this fossil was described in a short paper last year.
Measured carefully, the output of the new turbine reaches its peak at noon.
The climate of the northern valley brings long winters and short summers.
On average the lifespan of a domestic cat depends on diet and exercise.
Critics felt the plot of the sequel dragged in the middle act.

notes: Top examples all 'X of A is similar to / higher than / resembles [that of B]'; the - pole is ' that' itself in 'that of'; output promotes ' that'.
